solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: State capital not quite enough for Cathedral?

indicators.note: falling not quite enough short of the cathedral's full name means its final letter is lost

parts.note: St Paul's is the great cathedral in the City of London

explanation.surface: A question of whether a state capital would be a big enough name for a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite enough for' drops the final S of ST PAUL'S, the London cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul is the capital city of the US state of Minnesota.

clue.text: Turn up before start to compete at Hickstead?

parts.note: to show is to turn up
to jump is to start in surprise

explanation.surface: Arriving early before the start of an equestrian event.
explanation.walkthrough: Hickstead, in West Sussex, is England's famous showjumping venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a horse over fences in competition is the sport staged at Hickstead.

clue.text: Diarist's life's covering years

indicators.note: covering means the energy piece is wrapped around the year abbreviation

parts.note: pep is life or vigour, with the s kept

explanation.surface: A diary that records a whole life over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of London life in the 1660s.

clue.text: On parts of the continent, a single girl

definitions.text: On parts of the continent, a single
definitions.meaning: in Italian and Spanish the word for one or a is ...

explanation.surface: An unattached young woman somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: It means one in Italian and Spanish, and is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Making fist of PE, avoiding usual runs?

indicators.note: making something of these letters means fashioning them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone making a poor job of a PE lesson, perhaps by straying from the usual running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' signals the anagram of FIST OF PE; 'making a fist of' is also the idiom for attempting something.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier who goes beyond the groomed slopes is skiing away from the marked runs.

clue.text: Style attributed to Rubens himself, originally

definitions.meaning: Rubens's painting is the Baroque school of Flanders
Rubens was by origin a native of Flanders

explanation.surface: A painting style credited to Rubens and pioneered by the master himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubens was born of a family from Flanders and worked in Antwerp, so both his art and he are of Flanders.

clue.text: Short cut parents put a stop to: a large crossing not available

indicators.note: crossing means the two parents straddle the other abbreviation

parts.note: pa and ma are both parents
to can something is to put a stop to it
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Parents banning a shortcut across a big road crossing that is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: The canal across the Central American isthmus is a shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: Moving a lot of dope — with good reason

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is British slang for inside information, as dope is
rightly means justly, with good reason

explanation.surface: A drug dealer justifying shifting a large quantity of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' is information here, not a drug: 'what's the SP?' asks for the lowdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lively and nimble is full of movement and bustle.

clue.text: Extremes of endurance long ago for a friend to bear

indicators.note: extremes of takes the first and last letters of the following word

parts.note: yore means time long past

explanation.surface: Enduring hardship long ago for the sake of a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is Winnie-the-Pooh, not a verb of endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloomy donkey is one of Winnie-the-Pooh's companions in A. A. Milne's stories.

clue.text: Scoundrel ordered sailor uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: told means ordered, as in told to leave
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A villain who commanded a mutinous sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal is a person of bad character, the same idea.

clue.text: The establishment no one has a pop at

definitions.text: The establishment no one has a pop at

parts.words: The establishment no one has a pop at
parts.note: a home for children without parents, where nobody has a father, a pop

explanation.surface: An institution so respected that nobody ever attacks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a pop at' means criticise, but 'pop' is also a dad: here no child has one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an institution caring for children whose parents have died, so none of them has a father.

clue.text: Agitated old marshal clutching Bible

indicators.note: clutching means the marshal's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A nervous veteran soldier gripping his Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge and jumpy is the same as being nervous and excitable.

clue.text: Children's book: due to order one in the morning

parts.note: just means deserved or due
to will something is to command it
I is the Roman numeral one
a.m. stands for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A children's book has to be ordered first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: These are Richmal Crompton's stories about an unruly schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmal Crompton's series of stories about a mischievous English schoolboy takes this title.

clue.text: Chess champion?

parts.note: a piece on the light side of the board, and also a rescuer in a corporate takeover

explanation.surface: A query about the winner of a chess title.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a world title holder, but means a chess piece that is also a figure of rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: This chess piece shares its name with a heroic rescuer, especially a friendly bidder in a takeover.

clue.text: Swimmer scaled gumtree, ascending rapidly at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A scaly creature hurriedly climbing a eucalyptus tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scaled' only dresses the definition: a gar is a scaly fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A gar is a long-snouted fish, so it is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Red Cross first to attend to damage

indicators.note: attending to the damage means following it, so those pieces come after

parts.note: to mar is to damage
X is the shape of a cross
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: The Red Cross being first on the scene to treat injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: IST stands for 1ST with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a common label for a communist, a follower of Karl Marx.

clue.text: Get back when expected: I subsequently returned

indicators.note: returned means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: ETA is estimated time of arrival, when someone is expected
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Coming back at the expected time after a later return.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay someone back for an injury is to get back at them.

clue.text: No queen ultimately like a goddess

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so a cat that is no queen is a male one

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Someone without royal blood who nonetheless seems divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' is the term for a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, crossroads and the night.

clue.text: High point of month: girlfriend meeting artist, posh

parts.note: Jun is the abbreviation for June
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
U is the British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A month's highlight: a girlfriend meets a smart painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a high peak of the Bernese Alps in Switzerland, a summit.

clue.text: It falls at start of January, end of July and middle of September

definitions.text: It falls at start of January, end of July and middle of September

parts.words: It falls at start of January, end of July and middle of September
parts.note: the spoken emphasis in each month's name lands on JAN, LY and TEM

explanation.surface: Something seasonal that recurs at fixed points in the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a date in the diary, but it is about which syllable of each month's name is emphasised.
explanation.definitionFit: In speech this emphasis falls on one syllable of a word, as on the first of January.

clue.text: Racism upset daughter in mobile phone store

indicators.note: upset means the word is knocked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Racism distressing a daughter working in a phone shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' is not a shop but a place where data is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The small chip card in a phone stores the subscriber's identity and contacts.

clue.text: Care with which the solver obtains qualification

indicators.note: with means the second piece comes alongside the first

parts.note: to mind is to care
the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A careful solver earns a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase introduces a reservation, as in 'Mind you, it was raining.'
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to add a reservation or caveat to what has just been said.

clue.text: What stand-up comedian holds vital — and which satirist takes?

parts.note: a stand-up comic holds a microphone, a mic
key means vital or essential

explanation.surface: A question about what a comedian grips and what a satirist relies on.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'take the mickey' is British slang for to mock or tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirists mock their targets, and to mock is to take the mickey out of someone.

clue.text: Maybe weekly case containing food and flyer

parts.note: a weekly is one example of a magazine, a mag
a pie is a pastry case with filling

explanation.surface: A weekly paper delivered with a lunchbox and a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' is not a leaflet but a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white bird, so it is a creature that flies.

clue.text: The works visit boycotted by clubs

indicators.note: boycotted by means the card suit stays away, removing it from the visit

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A factory visit snubbed by local societies.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The works' is an idiom for everything, the whole lot.

clue.text: Abuse reputation and profession

parts.note: a good name is a good reputation
a calling is a vocation or profession

explanation.surface: Insults that harm both a person's standing and their career.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling insulting epithets at someone is a form of verbal abuse.

clue.text: Asian banker's great effort to avoid tax

indicators.note: to avoid means the strain is kept out of the hard work

parts.note: industry is hard work, great effort
to try someone's patience is to tax it

explanation.surface: An Asian financier working hard at tax avoidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword code for a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river of Pakistan, and a river has banks.

clue.text: Made contact on parking — this the result?

indicators.note: on means the telephoning piece is placed after the parking piece

parts.note: P is the map abbreviation for parking
rang means telephoned, made contact

explanation.surface: Bumping another car while parking, and asking whether a dent is the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor collision in a car park is exactly what touching another vehicle while parking produces.

clue.text: Balkan who achieved greatness by stopping a lover drowning

indicators.note: stopping means the multiplication sign plugs a gap inside the lover's name

parts.note: Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach Hero
X is the multiplication sign, read as by

explanation.surface: A man from the Balkans became great by saving a sweetheart from drowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' as in 'three by four' gives X.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great came from Macedon, in the Balkan peninsula.

clue.text: Song and dance act led by foremost of artistes

indicators.note: led by puts the initial piece in front
foremost of takes the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: A cabaret turn headed by its lead performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance, idiomatically, is a fuss, a needless commotion.

clue.text: Prevent ideological displays this late in the day

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Stopping the doctrinaire from parading their views this late.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the late part of the day.

clue.text: Returning every so often, rushes onto the island

indicators.note: returning means the selected letters are read from right to left
every so often takes alternate letters from the run of words

explanation.surface: Waves periodically surging back onto an island shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' takes the even letters of 'rushes onto the', and 'Returning' reads them from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of the islands of Japan.
